# HotReload / TestFramework / Debugger Contract V2 exhaustive audit

Date: 2026-08-24  
Mode: read-only source/runner contract review; no product, TestSource, OpenSpec, or plugin file was edited.  
Source aggregate SHA-256: `30bb1d953bd4cb0cbd22c61f264d4ba13692abe8f5cb12f78444b817bc2daf55`

## Result

All **250** source files and **489** parsed callables are represented. The exact-signature review marks **484** callables `reviewed-exact` and **5** `blocking-review-required`. The blockers are intentionally limited to Debugger source-line preservation and the deliberately broken last-good-generation fixture; they are not missing rows.

The current three-domain corpus has no forbidden legacy callable names and no `Expected*` parameters. Its main Contract V2 gap is that knowledge comments are at file scope instead of immediately attached to every callable. The proposed declaration remains exact unless a later source-level design explicitly adds raw snapshots; names used by registry, reflection, import linkage, delegate type identity, engine callbacks, or debugger lookup are recorded as required names rather than beautified.

`ownerQualifiedIdentity` is `owner|exact declaration`. Because HotReload intentionally repeats the same symbol in multiple source versions, global cross-version collisions are expected and retained in the JSON. The uniqueness gate uses `sourcePath|ownerQualifiedIdentity`, which is zero-duplicate.

## Contract rules frozen by this audit

1. Keep CaseId as data; use a semantic subcase and a separately recorded callable name.
2. Put the proposed English knowledge comment immediately above the first annotation/declaration for every callable.
3. Preserve registry leaves/hooks, lifecycle overrides, FName/reflection targets, imports, delegate/event types, and debugger lookup names with a non-empty required-name reason.
4. Return raw typed values. Record every `&out`/`&inout` channel separately. Expected values live in vectors, never in callable parameters.
5. HotReload vectors state ordered source version, provider/consumer role, reload result, retained objects, replaced descriptors/bodies/defaults, permission to invoke old objects, compile diagnostics, and failure-safe cleanup.
6. TestFramework vectors separate registry/discovery evidence from payload assertions and state suite instance, command/session, terminal path, and cleanup ownership.
7. Debugger declarations and line maps are one atomic contract. Per-callable comments must be inserted only with line-neutral source budgeting or matching C++/DAP expectation updates.

## High-risk retained/replaced matrices incorporated

### `BlueprintDelegatePropertyReloadsAfterInstanceRuntime` — `TS-HR-BLUEPRINT-DELEGATE-RUNTIME`

Retain the Blueprint-child instance and BeginPlay count through V1-V3; replace the delegate/property/function descriptors at V4, rebind the new signature, then clear the delegate and destroy actor, asset, world, and generations.

### `CDOAndInstanceConsistency` — `TS-HR-CDO-INSTANCE-CONSISTENCY`

The full-reload pair replaces UClass/CDO while an old leased CDO remains readable; the soft-reload pair retains class, CDO, instance, and Counter while replacing GetValue body behavior.

### `DefaultComponentMetadataAndRuntimeHierarchySurviveSoftReload` — `TS-HR-DEFAULT-COMPONENT-HIERARCHY`

Retain class, CDO, existing actor, RootScene, Billboard, and ReplacementBillboard identities; replace only GetVersion body and verify non-null registered component hierarchy on existing and fresh instances.

### `DelegateReceiverLifecycleBoundaryAcrossReload` — `TS-HR-DELEGATE-RECEIVER-LIFECYCLE`

Broadcast through the real event with a live receiver before and after body reload, then destroy the receiver and broadcast again; never call HandleSignal directly; clear bindings and tear down the world.

### `DoesNotReplayBeginPlayOnLiveActor` — `TS-HR-NO-BEGINPLAY-REPLAY`

Retain the live actor and class across soft reload; BeginPlayCount remains one and persistent state survives while GetValue behavior changes; a fresh actor may receive one new BeginPlay.

### `MulticastDelegateRuntimeRunsAcrossReloads` — `TS-HR-MULTICAST-RUNTIME`

Retain actor and multicast property while replacing handler bodies; expose raw counts after Broadcast, Unbind, and Clear, then clear all bindings before world teardown.

### `MultipleSoftReloadsUpdateRunningBlueprintChildFunction` — `TS-HR-BLUEPRINT-CHILD-SOFT-SEQUENCE`

Retain parent class, Blueprint child class, live instance, Value, and BeginPlayCount through V1-V4; replace function bodies and observe 10, 11, 31, and 40 in version order.

### `StructuralReloadKeepsExistingAndFreshBlueprintChildDefaults` — `TS-HR-BLUEPRINT-CHILD-STRUCTURAL-DEFAULTS`

Replace parent class/CDO on structural reload; distinguish old/new parent CDO, existing/fresh Blueprint CDO, and existing/fresh instances while preserving existing defaults and applying new defaults only to fresh objects.

### `SoftReloadKeepsBlueprintChildInstanceOnUpdatedParentBody` — `TS-HR-BLUEPRINT-CHILD-SOFT-BODY`

Retain parent class, Blueprint child class, and existing actor; replace GetValue body from 30 to 42 and verify a distinct fresh instance also returns 42.

## Implementation gates

- Regenerate inventory and require identical source file count and zero unmapped source-qualified callable identities before editing each batch.
- Reject `Observe_*`, `SurfaceNNN`, `_Nominal`, legacy forwarding aliases, `Expected*` parameters, and compound booleans as the only multi-value oracle.
- Require one immediately attached English comment per callable and preserve all required-name reasons.
- For HotReload, run version files strictly in the recorded order and assert retained/replaced identities plus explicit cleanup on success/failure.
- For framework discovery, assert exact suite/method/module/display identity and source-located diagnostics; do not infer coverage from leaf-body assertions.
- For Debugger, capture the C++/DAP expected locations first, then make comment insertion line-neutral or update expectations atomically; re-run exact debugger prefixes.
- Recompute per-source and aggregate SHA-256 after implementation so review can distinguish planned source changes from drift.
